title: Trip reach: do fed ants stop walking to an empty pile?
question: Colony bed, food 90 cells east of the nest (the nest is at the left), a small pile that refills every 6,000 frames. Same seed, the last 2,400 frames of a cycle, after the pile's last load went home. One colony counts food shuffled beside its own door as 'food still coming home'; the other counts only food carried in from out in the world, so its fed ants should stand down. Magenta = empty ant, cyan = carrying food. Which colony has stopped sending ants out to the empty pile -- and is the difference visible at all?
context_md: Counts, seed 14, frames 15,600-18,000 (one colony / the other, labels hidden): fed ants setting out 6 / 1; ants seen more than 26 cells out of the nest 10 / 5; mean drive of foragers 0.93 / 0.47. Over 24 seeds fed set-outs fall in every third of the cycle (96/119/173 -> 63/81/128), last third not significant by seed (10 higher / 12 lower). Food taken, starved and born do not move outside seed noise. Report: Reports/ant-scenes-2026-09-23.md s22u.
